Clients retry after a timeout; omitted includeHistory and false are the same semantic request; the same key with a different normalized body must be rejected. Cancellation is allowed only in queued or running, and polling must distinguish retryable and terminal failures without leaking backend topology. Keep the existing exported interfaces and legacyStartClientView compatible. Put any additional request/response, lifecycle, retry, and compatibility guidance or runnable examples in a separate owned artifact. Run maintained caller tests, demonstrate that they reject the original defective implementation, and restore the repair. Backend queue implementation is a separate responsibility.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The executable work stays at the caller contract boundary rather than building queue workers or persistence. The evaluator checks the hierarchy relationship (broader=developer-experience; children=graphql-engineering,grpc-protobuf,http-rest-engineering; near-neighbor=backend-engineering) from routing and delivery records; the candidate need not invent a skill-selection narrative.

The maintained artifact set defines request identity, replay response, legal lifecycle transitions, safe public failures, and installed-client behavior. contract-context.md remains the normative input; any extra schemas or runnable examples agree with it and with the existing in-process caller entry points.
A caller can decide whether to retry, cancel, or stop solely from the published contract; transport retries cannot create duplicate logical exports.

Use maintained contract tests and runnable examples for the semantic partitions this export contract actually exposes: a new start, same-key replay including omitted versus false normalization and current state, same-key/different-body rejection with one logical export, cancellation in queued/running and rejection without mutation in packaging/complete/cancelled/failed, missing-resource errors, retryable versus terminal failure polling, compatibility through the supplied older client, and recovery from an uncertain prior start. Assert values, classifications, identities, and observable state rather than only success flags or test names. Do not invent unrelated pagination, authorization-denial, or deprecation cases.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not expose persistence tables directly, return 200 for every semantic failure, add breaking fields/enum behavior casually, or force callers to reverse-engineer retryability.

contract-context.md remains at its original path with identical bytes. Implementation and maintained tests fulfill its promises; additional owned guidance does not weaken it. Editing, removing, moving, or regenerating the normative reference is an integrity failure.

tests/export-contract.test.ts passes against the repaired implementation and fails against the original defective src/export-contract.ts because a caller assertion detects a defect. Restore the repaired source afterward. Hidden checks, keyword-only tests, import failures, and a prose coverage list cannot substitute for maintained executable regression evidence. Rejection of one defect is not proof that all semantic partitions are covered.

Every material completion claim maps to changed artifacts and observed commands/results, with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled. The evaluator supplies hierarchy observations, paired run artifacts, and independent review records. Do not require the candidate to author those records or infer production queue durability from this local in-process fixture.
